items.title: Louis Cottrell, Jr. Interview, 1961-08-25
items.q: I think he was with Jelly Roll at the time

ctx.x: I knew his wife, I think his wife just died two or three years ago. Just about, just about. That's right. That's why I thought he died there too. Yeah, he did die over there. Did he go back to play on that trip? Can you remember?

Yeah, he went back. He was playing while he was up there, because I think he was with Jelly Roll at the time, or Woken in and out around at the time of his death. Because that's what he had gone back up there. Depression had set in after 29 and things that were going to get very slow and money was hard to get. Oh yeah, that's right. Depression was on there. So he went and he went by boat up there, because that was the cheaper way of transportation. He got up there. Now it's either 32 or 33. I don't recall exactly…

I was going to ask, it reminds me in New York, I heard years ago of rumors that he had sold some numbers to Ellington, like maybe he'd helped write Mood Indigo, you know, that slow blues type thing. And Barney Bigard once told me, I remember about the last time I saw Barney, when he was back with Louie at the time before the present time, in Chicago. And he said that T.O. had sold him several tunes, he thought. He'd written some of those things. Do you know of any of his composing activities or anything that he…
